findings.claim: With --instructions-root, a tracked instruction path that the pull request turns into a symlink pointing outside the repository counts as untracked and is read from the working tree, so a pull request can make --prompt-file read /proc/self/environ (the API key goes into the task, and from there into the report and the public PR comment) or make a --context folder point at /proc/self, so read_file can open the environ under --no-shell.

The agent and publish steps run `uv run --script` with the pull request's checkout as the working directory, and uv reads uv.toml or pyproject.toml [tool.uv] from there. A pull request that adds a uv.toml with its own index runs any code it likes in the step that holds the API key (or GH_TOKEN in publish), with no change to the workflow and no shell given to the agent.

publish_comment takes the first comment from any author whose body holds the marker. A person who quotes the marker in a comment makes every later publish PATCH a comment GITHUB_TOKEN cannot edit, so publish exits 1 on every push. Match only comments by the token's own user (github-actions[bot]).

Row r7 says --skills resolves under DIR, but test_instructions_root_resolves_tracked_paths never checks where the skills came from: both trees hold the same `review` skill, so the test still passes if --skills resolves against the current folder.
